hidden-past.title: Whose Arrest Does This Famous 1914 Photo Really Show?
hidden-past.description:
A photograph from Sarajevo, 1914, is often captioned as the arrest of Gavrilo Princip. Several scholars say it shows a bystander, Ferdinand Behr. Sources and image credits are below.

#Shorts #History #WW1 #Sarajevo #HiddenPast

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Archduke_Franz_Ferdinand
- https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ferdinand_Behr_arrested_in_Sarajevo_1914.jpg
- The New York Times, 29 June 1914, via Wikimedia Commons / Internet Archive

Images: Wikimedia Commons (Imperial War Museums and others).

ai-tested.title: Can AI Count Letters? We Tested Two Models
ai-tested.description:
We gave OpenAI's GPT-OSS and Google's Gemini Flash-Lite the same 20 letter-counting questions, and code marked every reply. One test, run on 9 November 2026. Results can change between runs and as models update.

#Shorts #AI #AITested #Gemini #TechNews

hidden-past-berlin.title: The Announcement That Came Too Early: Berlin Wall, 1989
hidden-past-berlin.description:
On 9 November 1989 an East German spokesman, handed a note and not fully briefed, said new travel rules took effect immediately. That night the checkpoints opened. Facts from Wikipedia's account of the fall of the Berlin Wall; photos from Wikimedia Commons with credits in the video.

#Shorts #History #BerlinWall #ColdWar #HiddenPast

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Berlin_Wall
Images: Bundesarchiv (CC BY-SA 3.0 de), Günter Schabowski (CC BY-SA 3.0) and a public-domain photograph, via Wikimedia Commons.
